subject: AcmeBank - data residency & region pinning follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acmebank.com>, Bob Lee <bob.lee@acmebank.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 14:23:00 -0700
Subject: AcmeBank kickoff - data residency & region pinning (post-call recap)

Hi Alice / Bob -

Thanks again for the call today - really helpful to understand the AcmeBank integration patterns and your compliance constraints. Quick recap and next steps on the items we covered around data residency / logging / cross-region behavior: 

1) Region pinning: you mentioned all PII and sensitive customer content must be stored and processed in the customer-controlled US region. We confirmed Redwood can pin inference workloads to a specific region (e.g., us-east-1) and avoid cross-region processing for primary inference requests.

2) Cross-region failover: you want automatic failover for availability but only if data does not leave the US. We noted Redwood supports configurable failover policies - we can failover within the same region to another AZ or to a dedicated instance in the same region; cross-region failover can be configured but requires encryption-at-rest key residency and contractual approval.

3) Backups & DR: backups for model artifacts and logs are encrypted and we can restrict backup storage residency to the US. We'll need to confirm retention windows and whether you require us to delete backups after a retention period or retain in archived form per your policy.

4) Logging / audit: request/response logs (for debugging and quality monitoring) can be redacted/disabled for PII fields. We can also provide audit logs and a schema of what we retain (timestamps, routing metadata, token counts, but not full unredacted PII unless allowed).

Attachments: I'm attaching a short diagram of our region-pinning architecture and a one-pager SOC2 summary for your security team.

Next steps / asks:
- Can you confirm whether your legal/security team requires written contractual language for key residency and backup location?
- Which retention window do you expect for logs and backups (e.g., 90 / 365 days)?
- Would you like a dedicated technical deep-dive on region pinning with Aditya next week?

If useful, I can schedule a 30-min follow-up - Aditya is happy to walk through the diagram and specific KMS/HSM options.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments:
- redwood_region_pinning_diagram.pdf (architecture diagram, 1 page)

From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acmebank.com>

Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 16:10:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: AcmeBank kickoff - data residency & region pinning (post-call recap)

Thanks Marissa - appreciate the recap and the diagrams. A couple clarifying items from our security team after reviewing the diagram: 

- When you say "pin to region" can you confirm there is no chance of any inference traffic being routed through non-US regions (even for health checks, telemetry, or telemetry-based batching)? Specifically, we need assurances that latent telemetry packets or probe traffic do not cross borders.

- For cross-region failover: our preference is failover inside the US only. If you support multi-region deployments for resilience, we need explicit control that failover cannot go to EU/APAC without prior sign-off. What is the configuration surface for that?

- Backups: we need the ability to specify the retention policy per-tenant and a documented deletion process (time to delete / proof of deletion). Can you provide S3 bucket naming/location patterns and whether snapshots are geo-replicated by default?

- Logs: can you provide a sample audit log schema and confirm whether request/response logs are stored in plaintext anywhere by default? What redaction options exist (pre-send redaction, sampling, or suppression)?

We'd like Aditya to do a technical dive on Monday or Tuesday next week (US Eastern morning).

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Johnson
Senior Cloud Security Engineer | AcmeBank
alice.johnson@acmebank.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acmebank.com>, Bob Lee <bob.lee@acmebank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 08:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AcmeBank kickoff - data residency & region pinning (post-call recap)

Hi Alice - quick technical answers below; happy to expand in a call and share configuration screenshots.

1) "Pin to region" behavior:
- Primary inference ingress, model execution, KV cache, and temporary transient storage for requests are all confined to the pinned region (e.g., us-east-1) when you select region-pin mode.
- Health checks and control-plane telemetry are configurable: by default some lightweight telemetry (metrics, error rates) flows to our control plane for multi-tenant observability; we can enable a "privacy-first" mode that routes telemetry to a customer-controlled collector in the same region or suppresses it entirely.

2) Cross-region failover:
- Failover policies are explicit: you (AcmeBank) can choose {"same-region-failover-only", "same-country", "explicit-allowed-regions"}. The default for enterprise installations is "same-region-failover-only". Cross-region failover requires explicit opt-in and also KMS key residency confirmation.

3) Backups & replication:
- Backups are stored in customer-scoped buckets we provision within the chosen cloud region. By default we do not geo-replicate snapshots across regions. Geo-replication is an opt-in feature and would need contractual approval.
- We support per-tenant retention policy configuration (e.g., 90/180/365 days) and provide explicit delete APIs; we also produce a deletion audit that includes bucket/object keys and timestamps.

4) Logging / redaction:
- Audit log schema (example fields): timestamp, request_id, route, model_version, token_count, client_account_id, action, status_code.
- Request/response bodies containing user PII are NOT stored in plaintext unless you enable full request logging. We offer three modes: "full", "redacted" (PII fields masked), and "none" (no request/response body stored).

I'll prepare a short tech note with the config flags and KMS options before our call. If you can confirm a time Monday 9:30-10:00am ET, I will book a Zoom and include configuration screenshots.

-Aditya
